title: Is Maida Harmful? The Truth About All Purpose Flour
tags: why is maida bad for you
description:
Kerala porotta, naan, samosas, cakes, bread, and pizzas—so many of our favorite foods are made from maida (refined flour). Yet maida is constantly demonized as “poison,” “empty calories,” or even a cause of diabetes and cancer. But is maida really harmful, or is this just another case of fear mongering fueled by chemophobia and pseudoscience?

In this episode of Pale Blue Thoughts, we explore the science behind maida. We explain what maida actually is—the endosperm of wheat—and how it’s processed. We break down myths about bleaching with benzoyl peroxide, which is an approved, safe chemical also used in medicines and dental products, and why fear of “chemicals” ignores the fact that everything around us, even water and air, is chemical. We also tackle claims about alloxan, “stickiness in the intestines,” and diabetes, and show why these arguments fall apart when tested against real evidence.

If you’ve searched for “is maida harmful, Kerala porotta health facts, maida vs atta, does maida cause diabetes, maida myths”, this video gives you the scientific perspective. Maida is mostly carbohydrates, which give your body energy. Eaten in moderation and combined with proteins, vegetables, and exercise, it is no more harmful than rice or other carbs. The real danger comes from misinformation spread by blogs, media, and YouTubers chasing clicks.

Enjoy your porotta guilt-free, because science says maida isn’t the villain it’s made out to be. Don’t forget to like, share, comment, and subscribe for more myth-busting, science-backed content.

In a typical Indian's diet generally we see a huge plate of rice along with either non-veg curry or multiple vitamin packed subzis on the side. If they're from the north, the rice gets replaced by 4-5 Rotis or other breads. The point I'm trying to make here is that our diet is 70% carbs/glucose and 30% Proteins, vitamins, minerals etc. Couple the with lack of exercise and this leads increased Blood sugar, higher fat build up and minimal muscle growth or even muscle loss.

Now that we have established that, let's take the making of Maida.. we take nutritious whole wheat, stripping of its nutritious layer filled with proteins, oil etc which we struggle to get from our typical diet, and since we have taken the protective outer layer of Wheat we then need to artificially bleach it to protect it's inside. Yes, taste is subjective, there are people who prefer whole wheat over maida and vice versa... but why make a video that's biased and that would spread more confusion...
